sources.headline: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
sources.text: Figure caption, Footage shows Ukrainian missile approach Crimea bridgeByOlivia IrelandSarah RainsfordSouthern and Eastern Europe correspondent, Kyiv and Ilya AbishevBBC News RussianUpdated 2 hours agoUkraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort.The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before".Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partially resumed on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - after they had been closed following Russian strikes overnight.Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin.The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014. The $3.6bn (£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018.Image source, Anadolu Agency/Getty ImagesImage caption, Putin (centre) personally opened the Crimean Bridge by driving a lorry over it in May 2018In Ukraine, the much-hated bridge is seen as one of the main symbols of Russia's continuing occupation of Ukrainian lands."We're drinking champagne!" Andrii, an engineer who lives in Kyiv, told the BBC.He said the latest attack would "deal a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians".Some Ukrainians are concerned that Putin might now respond by carrying out even more attacks against civilian infrastructure, but Andrii said: "I don't think the Russians can make things much worse; they're already pounding us every single night with everything they've got."Image caption, Images show the damage to the Crimean Bridge from the overnight attackThe damage after the overnight attack, involving cruise missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section apparently destroyed.Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below.Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective".He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage".The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed. Ukraine's state security service SBU said its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders".Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch.The Kremlin said Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China.Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations".For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday.Figure caption, Watch: BBC reports from Kyiv bridge hit by Russian attackIn Kyiv, loud explosions were heard just before midnight on Monday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies.On Tuesday, Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had targeted the Southern Bridge, and another three had been fired on the Northern Bridge.Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were also damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters.Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River, connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city.Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials.The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear, though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly.The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired.However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar.This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack.Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk.Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control.Additional reporting by Jaroslav Lukiv

sources.headline: How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule
sources.text: At 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.The Ukrainian drone that was involved in the latest attack on Kerch bridge. Writing in Cyrilic says: ‘We will stand, Moscow will fall.’ Photograph: “Leon”/Magyar’s BirdsTypically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months the work had become almost mundane: they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions.“We knew what the target was. Everyone was enthusiastic and excited,” one person who took part in the special operation, using the pseudonym “Leon”, told the Guardian. His 7th Deep Strike Centre is part of “Magyar’s Birds”, a brigade named after the call sign of its founder, Robert Brovdi, the head of Ukraine’s unmanned systems forces. Leon said: “Nobody gets excited any more about oil refineries. This was different.”The soldiers got ready to launch, then watched the biplane-like drone, laden with explosives, disappear across the southern Ukrainian steppe.Ukraine releases footage of strike on Crimean Bridge – videoOver the next four hours, hundreds of attack drones followed the same linear path, flying first over land and then over the Black Sea. In the early hours of the morning they arrived at their destination: the Kerch bridge connecting occupied Crimea with Russia. Putin opened the monumental road and rail crossing in 2018, driving across it in a Kamaz truck. This was four years after his undercover troops – known as little green men – seized the peninsula.President Putin speaks with workers as he inspects the road section of the Kerch bridge in 2018. Photograph: Alexei Nikolsky/Pool Sputnik Kremlin/APRussian propagandists had described the bridge as impregnable. It was, they said, an edifice as strong and unyielding as their country’s iron leader. For Ukraine, by contrast, it was a hated symbol of Russian arrogance and colonial thinking. Also, officials pointed out, it was illegal. Twice Kyiv had tried to blow it up – with a truck bomb in 2022, and a sea drone the following year.On this occasion, the Ukrainian military’s careful, multi-stage plan worked perfectly. “It was a well-coordinated operation. Waves of drones started from different locations. The goal was to overwhelm Russia’s well-organised air defence system, rather than the bridge itself,” Leon explained.As expected, the initial salvo tied up Russia’s local defences. According to insiders, Ukraine then launched a second drone wave. Its function was crucial and different: to act as a relay system for radio signals. Previously, Ukrainian units had used Starshield, the military equivalent of Starlink, for mid-range strikes on occupied territory. Elon Musk’s SpaceX owns the satellite internet network, which is overseen by the Pentagon and the Trump administration.A satellite image of the Kerch bridge. Photograph: Vantor/ReutersTen days ago, however, limits were mysteriously imposed on Ukrainian drones, so they could no longer fly at above 161 km/h (100 mph). SpaceX insists there is no slowdown – a statement Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, says is untrue. On Monday night, it appears Kyiv bypassed US restrictions by setting up its own extraordinary and innovative real-time video and radio connection.Once the relay was in place, a third wave of attacks could begin. This time they featured Flamingos, a potent Ukrainian-made cruise missile capable of carrying 1,000kg of explosives – enough to seriously damage the bridge. An unknown number of missiles – some reports say at least four – were launched from southern Ukraine and sent towards Crimea.A video from one of the Flamingos shows it drawing inexorably towards the target. The onboard camera captures a ghostly night-time scene. The crossing looms into view against a grisaille background. Suddenly a gigantic steel arch appears. The feed cuts out. Other footage shows the moment of impact: an orange fireball, pricking the surrounding blackness.Photos taken on Tuesday morning in the aftermath of the attack show a scene of watery devastation. A massive arch had tumbled overnight into the Kerch straight, with a large concrete chunk of the road crossing. Nobody will be driving across the bridge anytime soon. The adjacent railway arch span was also damaged. “We were very happy, swapping messages all night,” Leon said.A drone view of what appears to be smoke rising and explosions at the Kerch bridge. Photograph: Security Service Of Ukraine/ReutersOne source in Ukraine’s armed forces said the timing of the operation – hailed by Zelenskyy as “unprecedented” – was deliberate. It was conducted ahead of a meeting on Thursday between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Putin in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of an Apec summit. “The bridge is a symbol of Putin’s rule. Destroying it sends a message to the other two great leaders that Putin is not as strong as he pretends,” the person said.They added: “We understand that what we did shows the world that the king is nude. Putin is weak and vulnerable and we just proved it. The operation was purposefully designed for this specific historic moment. Putin’s plan was to bluff at the summit about how powerful he is. In reality, he can’t even protect the most important and symbolic pillars of his regime.”A grab taken from a video released by the Ukrainian security service showing damage to the bridge. Photograph: Telegram/@V_Zelensky_official/AFP/Getty ImagesIn addition to Putin’s political embarrassment before his peers, the disabling of the Kerch bridge has practical consequences. Since annexing Crimea, Russia has militarised the peninsula, effectively turning it into a giant and fortified army base. Since 2022 it has been used as a launch platform for drone and missile attacks on the port of Odesa, and other Ukrainian cities in the region.Russia’s occupying southern army has relied on the bridge for regular deliveries of ammunition, equipment and fuel. With the crossing partially closed – rail travel reportedly reopened on Tuesday – Russia will have to use an under fire land corridor instead, connecting its Rostov oblast with the Moscow-controlled parts of Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia and Kherson provinces.Map showing the Kerch bridge“We have disrupted their logistics to Crimea. There will be a lot of problems for Russia’s army in the south,” Leon predicted. Debris from the bridge strike is obstructing the narrow shipping corridor through the Kerch strait, linking the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea. The Azov sea now resembles a lake. Passenger ferries are unable to move, with the occupied ports of Mariupol and Berdyansk cut off.The soldiers returned from their mission jubilant and elated. Back at their headquarters, they gathered as usual for a minute’s silence, in memory of those killed in Russia’s bloody war. “We had our daily ritual as usual. Then there were congratulations on a very successful and important operation,” Leon said. Then he added: “We are paying them back.”

sources.headline: Ukraine Attacks Kerch Bridge Linking Russia to Occupied Crimea
sources.text: Destroying the structure, the only one connecting Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, has long been a top objective for Kyiv.

sources.headline: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate
sources.text:
A freight train runs on rails of a railway link of the Crimean Bridge connecting Russian mainland and the Crimean Peninsula over the Kerch Strait not far from Kerch, Crimea, on July 17, 2023.
AP
hide caption
AP
KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian drones and missiles struck the vital Kerch Bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday, calling it an "unprecedented" operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.
Zelenskyy portrayed the bridge operation as a masterstroke following a weekslong effort by Ukrainian forces to gradually wear down Russian air defenses before bombarding the prized target with a barrage of missiles and drones overnight. Zelenskyy didn't detail the damage, but the Ukrainian General Staff said that an arch and a span of the bridge's road section collapsed, severing the road link, while the railway line was still standing but with a damaged arch. Russia's Investigative Committee, the nation's top criminal investigation agency, said the bridge was attacked by drones and sustained damage but didn't elaborate.
The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and for supporting troops on the front line. The construction of the bridge, a potent symbol of Russia's illegal annexation of the peninsula in 2014, was inflammatory to Ukrainians. "The symbol of the occupation has cracked," the Ukrainian General Staff said in a statement. Moscow's forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, hitting two of the Ukrainian capital's main bridges and killing at least two people. A recent escalation in aerial attacks came as Russia and Ukraine await a date for the next round of U.S.-mediated talks aimed at ending the war that began with Moscow's full-scale invasion of its neighbor on Feb. 24, 2022. U.S. President Donald Trump says he plans to talk about the war in Ukraine during his highly anticipated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China this week. Missiles delivered the final blow in the 7-stage operation The Kerch Bridge attack was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, Zelenskyy said on social media.
Ukrainian forces knocked out defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other designated targets before launching Monday night's final attack, he said. Domestically developed long-range drones struck the bridge's road section during the night while Ukraine's Neptune missiles and other drones aimed at the rail section, he said. Precision-guided Flamingo missiles delivered the final blow, he said. Zelenskyy and the Ukrainian military published videos showing what they said were the attacks and subsequent damage to the bridge, with part of the deck in the water and a fallen arch. The Associated Press wasn't able to verify the images.
The Russian-installed governor of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said traffic across the bridge was halted but rail traffic was restored by Tuesday afternoon. He didn't mention any damage. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that "there is no doubt that the bridge will be restored and will be even better than it was before." Zelenskyy noted that Russia has battered Ukrainian infrastructure, especially the power grid, every day. There were significant power outages Tuesday in three Ukrainian regions, he said. "We have repeatedly offered Russia steps toward de-escalation — and every proposal has been met with loud rejection," he said. U.K. Defense Secretary Wes Streeting, meeting at NATO headquarters in Brussels with Ukraine's Western backers, said the Kerch Bridge strike was "another example of Ukrainian ingenuity and Ukraine's absolute determination to defend itself against Russian aggression." The United Kingdom announced £240 million ($317 million) in air defense support for Ukraine this winter, including more than 1,000 short-range missiles and more than a dozen radars. Russian air defenses downed 1,441 drones during a second straight night of major Ukrainian attacks, Russia's Defense Ministry said Tuesday. That was a day after Russia said that it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones in the highest number of interceptions it had reported so far during the war. Ukraine also attacks industrial areas deep inside Russia Elsewhere, authorities in Bashkortostan, a Russian region in the southern Ural Mountains, said that defenses repelled a "massive" drone attack on industrial zones in the cities of Ufa and Salavat. All plants there worked as usual, officials said. However, independent news outlet Astra reported a huge fire at the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining and petrochemical complex in Bashkortostan, nearly 1,300 kilometers (800 miles) east of the Ukrainian border. The major petrochemical complex has been attacked a number of times before. In Moscow, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that around 800 drones flew toward the Moscow region overnight. Most were downed far away, and 321 were shot down as they approached the Russian capital.
Russia hits bridges in Ukraine's capital
Workers cut electrical wires on the southern bridge, damaged in a Russian missile strike, in Kyiv, Ukraine, Tuesday.
Evgeniy Maloletka/AP
hide caption
Evgeniy Maloletka/AP
Seven Russian ballistic missiles hit two of Kyiv's main bridges during the night, Zelenskyy said. Both were closed to traffic. The Pivnichnyi and Pivdennyi bridges are key commuter routes across the Dnipro River connecting Kyiv's two banks. The left bank is largely residential with numerous apartment buildings and shopping malls. The old town and many government offices are on the right bank. On Tuesday morning, long lines of traffic formed on a third bridge linking the two sides of the city. Russian attacks damaged other infrastructure and started fires in four districts of the Ukrainian capital, officials said, as Moscow continued its campaign to make life difficult for Ukrainian civilians. The Russian Defense Ministry said Tuesday that its forces overnight hit Ukraine's military industrial facilities, energy, transport and port infrastructure, as well as vessels used for Ukrainian armed forces. Russian forces launched a combined attack on industrial facilities in three districts of the southern Ukraine region of Zaporizhzhia, killing two people and wounding 18 others and leaving a large number of consumers in the region without power, local authorities said. The possibility of more talks Meanwhile, the negotiating teams of Ukraine, the United States, and European partners held a working video call Monday in which they discussed the results of recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, and the agenda for the next stage of negotiations, said Rustem Umerov, head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service. "We aligned our positions and our next joint steps," Umerov said on Telegram following the conversation. Representatives of France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Poland, NATO and the European Commission joined the conversation. The United States was represented by envoys Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and Alexus Grynkewich, the commander of U.S. forces in Europe, Umerov said.

Ukraine damages Russia’s Crimean bridge in major strike

Reuters
Published: 9:21pm, 17 Nov 2026Updated: 10:40pm, 17 Nov 2026

Ukrainian drones and missiles destroyed the central road section of the bridge linking Russia and Crimea on Tuesday, inflicting a military and symbolic blow on President Vladimir Putin two days before he is due to meet the leaders of China and the United States.

Videos and images posted on social media by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and verified by Reuters showed the bridge’s main road arch had crumbled into the sea, leaving a yawning gap.

“Russia strikes our infrastructure every day, including bridges,” Zelensky said. “We are … reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began.”

A video screengrab released on Tuesday shows damage to the Crimean bridge (Kerch bridge) that links Crimea to Russia, near Kerch. Photo: Ukrainian Security Service / AFP

The ‌19km (12-mile) bridge is a flagship project inaugurated by Putin in 2018 and a symbol of Russia’s attachment to the peninsula it captured and annexed from Ukraine in 2014.

The timing was awkward for the Kremlin leader ahead of his meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday with US President Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping, where the three are expected to discuss the Ukraine war among other topics.

Zelensky said the strike followed an unprecedented operation that methodically destroyed Russian air defences, radar systems and electronic warfare capabilities.

Sergei Aksyonov, Crimea’s Russian-installed governor, said two people were killed and road traffic had been suspended. Rail traffic partially resumed after a pause.

Putin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov said a repair plan would be prepared, making the bridge “even better than before”.

But Russian military bloggers said repairs would be exceptionally challenging given Ukraine’s capacity for further attacks.

Finnish ⁠military analyst Emil Kastehelmi posted on social media: “The road bridge won’t be repaired during this war … Ukraine has achieved a victory with both concrete and symbolic implications.”

The bridge over the Kerch Strait was once a key supply route for Russian ‌forces in Ukraine, but the military now relies more heavily on a land corridor running through parts of eastern and southern Ukraine that Russia has captured since launching a full-scale war with its neighbour in 2022.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin said a government commission had met to decide on steps to assess damage, launch repairs and discuss the ‌logistics of delivering cargo to Crimea via alternative routes.

A goods train runs on rails of a railway link of the bridge connecting the Russian mainland and Crimean peninsula over the Kerch Strait in July 2023. Photo: AP

The bridge spans a channel used by commercial vessels entering and leaving the Sea of Azov, making it an important part of ⁠the region’s grain export network.

While Black Sea grain ⁠shipments have largely stalled amid escalating drone attacks, export infrastructure has suffered limited damage, meaning trade could resume quickly if security conditions improve.

Andrey Sizov, of consultancy Sovecon, said the bridge’s collapse could “substantially delay any eventual resumption of shipping from the Sea of Azov” because debris would have to be cleared ‌from the channel.

Ukraine has attacked the bridge several times during the war. A truck bomb in October 2022 killed four people and limited the bridge’s capacity for several months. In July 2023, a section of road bridge was destroyed and a couple crossing by car were killed.

The overnight ‌attack was part of what Russian state media called Ukraine’s biggest drone attack yet. Russia said it shot down 1,441 drones over 22 regions, surpassing the previous record of 1,336 set on Monday.

Air defences repelled a major ‌drone attack on the industrial cities of Ufa and Salavat in Russia’s Bashkortostan region, home to several oil refineries, state media reported, citing local officials. Ukraine said it had hit a refinery and petrochemical complex in Salavat.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin ⁠said about 800 Ukrainian drones had flown towards the surrounding Moscow region, 321 of which had been brought down en route.

The scale and frequency of Ukrainian drone attacks have increased as Russia has intensified its own ⁠drone and missile campaign in a grinding war of attrition, with both sides targeting energy infrastructure and other strategic assets.

Attacks have continued despite US-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi last week, the first in nine months, and separate meetings between US envoys and Putin and Zelensky.

Kyiv and Moscow agreed on a major exchange of prisoners during last week’s talks but there was no significant breakthrough on broader issues, ‌including territory. Russia holds about a fifth of Ukrainian land ‌but the front line has remained largely static for months.

Workers inspect the North bridge damaged by a Russian missile strike, in Kyiv, Ukraine, on Tuesday. Photo: AP

In Kyiv, Reuters witnesses reported a series of loud explosions in the capital overnight.

Vitali Klitschko, Kyiv’s mayor, said Russia struck the city’s North and South bridges, an assertion later confirmed by Moscow, and partially damaged the metro system. The attacks caused some power and water outages and prompted transport restrictions, he said.

Overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure left consumers without power in eight Ukrainian regions, Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov said.

Russia said its forces had struck transport, military and energy facilities in Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, Cherkasy and Dnipropetrovsk, along with port infrastructure and a cargo ship.

Reuters could not immediately independently confirm the reports. Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians.
